music-sequencer-for-v2.note: Author-planted tripwire: the shipped .epe contains a deliberately invalid line the user is instructed to delete before running. Without stripping it the ORIGINAL fails to compile on every rig (`unknown identifier REMOVE_THIS_INVALID_LINE_IF_YOU_UNDERSTAND_THIS_WARNING`), so no side-by-side comparison is possible. See tools/verify/results/music-sequencer-for-v2.json.

music-sequencer-for-v3-only.note: Same author tripwire, v3 flavour: the .epe ships deliberately invalid sentinel LINES (plural — the verdict JSON only names the first; the second surfaces once the first is gone) that the user must delete. Unstripped, the ORIGINAL never compiles. See tools/verify/results/music-sequencer-for-v3-only.json.

nano-orbital.note: SWEEP-NOTES.md 'Manifest rig fixes needed': the original writes a fixed 144-px canvas and throws `array index out of bounds` at frame 0 on any rig under 144 px (bisected: fails <=128, fails at frame 13 @140, clean >=144).

nyan-lights.note: SWEEP-NOTES.md 'Manifest rig fixes needed': the original is an index-only 60x5 = 300-px sprite LUT, so the rig should be 300 px (16x16 renders it as a mosaic; it errors at >=324 px). 300 is not a whole multiple of a 16-wide grid, so the rig kind moves to strip as well.

orv-christmas-tree.note: SWEEP-NOTES.md 'Manifest rig fixes needed': the original renders only at pixelCount multiples of 20, so the rig should be grid 20x20 (the default 16x16 errors at frame 0).

performance-test-framework.nonVisual: The ORIGINAL is a CPU benchmark, not an animation: its render body is the comment `//sorry, no blinkenlights!` and its results are read through PB's Vars Watch, so all-black is the correct output on a real Pixel Blaze too. Pixel fidelity is therefore not a target and no verdict/score is meaningful — the pair stays in pairs.json (gen-pairs.mjs would re-add it anyway) but is excluded from the scored population.
performance-test-framework.note: Gitea #123, from the #108 silent-null diagnosis. The 2026-08 sweep filed this as `orig-unrenderable` after ten runs proving the original is black on every rig, fps, seed, wall clock and skip — correct observation, wrong bucket: the original does not FAIL on our engine, it succeeds at drawing nothing. The port deliberately adds a phase/progress readout the original never had (see the header of library/performance-test-framework.js); that is a documented deviation for the playground, not a scored defect, because there is nothing to be faithful to. Do not hand this slug to a judge.
